data.name: Verify_Header
data.value: Compare an image with a device

data.name: Verify_MethodText
data.value: Every byte of the image is compared with the device. The device is read directly, bypassing the Windows cache, so the data really comes from the media; archives are unpacked on the fly. SHA-256 of both sides is calculated as well.

data.name: Verify_ExpandNote
data.value: If the last partition was expanded after writing, differences in the partition table and in that partition's file system metadata are expected.

data.name: Verify_MoreRanges
data.value: Only the first {0} of {1} areas are listed.

data.name: Erase_Warning
data.value: Erasing destroys all partitions and data on the selected device. It cannot be undone.

data.name: Erase_QuickDescription
data.value: Clears the partition tables and file system signatures, then creates a new file system. Takes seconds. The old data physically stays on the media and can be recovered with special software.

data.name: Erase_FullDescription
data.value: Writes zeros over the whole device once, then creates a new file system, like a full format in Windows. The old data can no longer be recovered by software.

data.name: Erase_SecureDescription
data.value: Overwrites every sector with a pattern and then reads the whole device back. Destroys the data and tests the media at the same time: finds bad sectors and counterfeit cards with fake capacity. The device is written and read in full, so this takes the longest.

data.name: Erase_PatternDescription
data.value: Random data differs in every sector, so the check proves that each sector really keeps its own data. Zeros cannot reveal a card that wraps addresses around.

data.name: Erase_VerifyDescription
data.value: Read the whole device after writing and compare it with the pattern
